title: Miracle flower
text:
The miracle flower is a special kind of flower which grows very quickly.

At the start of day 1, it has a single bud.
By the end of day 1, a stalk with two new buds has grown from the initial bud.
On day 2, the process repeats: by the end of the day, a stalk with two new buds grows from each bud that developed the previous day.
This process continues day after day, with each bud from the previous day growing into a new stalk with two new buds by the end of the day.

As a result, the miracle flower becomes taller and more magnificent with each passing day.

Start of Day 1	End of Day 1	End of Day 2

	
	

 

After a number of days, the miracle flower looks like this:

Task

Calculate how many days this miracle flower took to grow.

Type a whole number and click save.

title: Ricca cards
text:
Barbara collects cards with monsters, the "Riccas". Here are her Ricca cards:

A card shows the properties of a Ricca, for example the name () or whether the Ricca has teeth (). Properties have values. On card 2, for example,  has the value MONI, and  has the value . The Ricca on the card is therefore called MONI and has teeth.

Barbara realises that there are only three different types of values on the cards. She calls them "data types":

	 Text, several letters in a row. 
	 Numbers, i.e. 1, 2, 3. 
	 The characters  and , which mean "yes" and "no".

Task

Assign the properties to the correct data types. 
Drag the value types to the boxes underneath the properties. Click save when you are done.

title: Superbebras
text:
In a computer game, the background consists of a sequence of tiles. Each tile is one of 4 different options.

The system continuously adds a new tile to the right of the current background sequence, and simultaneously removes a tile from the left. In this way, the computer creates the illusion of movement.

	


The system selects a new tile to add to the background using the rules illustrated in the diagram on the right. 

The ‘current tile’ is the one that is currently at the extreme right of the background sequence. It can be any of the 4 possible tiles, as shown opposite. The arrows indicate which is a valid selection for the ‘next tile’. A valid ‘next tile’  is one that is directly connected by a single straight or curved arrow to the ‘current tile’.

	

For example, if this tile is currently the final tile in the background sequence: 

the system could:

either select another identical tile (by following the curved arrow)  

Or select this tile: (by following the left arrow) 

Task

Using these rules, one of the following images is not a valid background sequence in the game. Select the invalid sequence.

title: Returning books
text:
Next please!

The beavers in Holzdorf are avid readers, which is why there are usually lots of beavers queuing at the library's return desk. The following rule applies:

The beaver with the fewest books to return goes next.

The librarian always needs exactly one

minute to process the return of each book. Once they have processed all the books returned by a beaver, the next beaver from the waiting area takes their turn and has all their books processed. It is always the beaver in the waiting area with the fewest books to return who goes next.

	

One morning, 5 beavers come to return their books. The table shows the arrival time and the number of books each beaver wants to return.

Name	Time of arrival	Number of books
Ana	9:00	4
Beti	9:02	6
Cene	9:03	2
Darja	9:05	4
Emil	9:11	1

 

Ana arrives first and can immediately return her 4 books.

Task

Work out what order the beavers get to return their books.

Drag the names into the correct position. Click save when you are done.
